newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Folgado said no need for 1997 mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Folgado said no need for 1997 mini-budget.

text.p: Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said on Wednesday that there was no need for a mini-budget later this year.

"We do not believe a mini-budget is necessary, however, given the government's commitment to fulfilling the deficit objective, corresponding measures would be adopted (if necessary) without allowing any type of budgetary 'hole'," Folgado told the legislature's economy committee.
He added that the government is systematically following the budget's execution to ensure that any deviations are detected and "necessary corrective measures" are taken.

In an appearance centred on last year's budget performance, Folgado declined to make forecasts on any possible deviations in revenues this year but he added that if revenues did not behave as expected "compensatory measures will be taken to achieve the objective."
The budget foresees non-financial revenues of 16.1 trillion pesetas, compared to 14.6 trillion in 1995. Expenditures are seen at 18.1 trillion compared with 18.3 trillion in 1995.
Folgado reiterated that Spain had fulfilled the deficit objective for all public administrations in 1996 of 4.4 percent of gross domestic product compared with 6.6 percent in 1995.
In 1996, the deficit for the state was 3.3 percent, compared to a forecast of 3.5 percent, 0.5 percent for Social Security compared with 0.3 percent forecast, and 0.6 for regional administrations.
